name: Infineon Technologies AG
thesis: Infineon is the European semiconductor leader in power systems and automotive chips, uniquely positioned across the AI data center power supply chain from the power grid to processor-adjacent vertical voltage regulator modules (VRMs achieving >3.0 A/mm²). The thesis seeds highlight an order backlog near €30B, AI data center power revenue accelerating toward >€2.5B in FY26 (up from >€1.6B in FY25), and multi-year capacity reservation agreements with hyperscalers. Independent evaluation, however, must weigh AI power tailwinds against cyclical realities: automotive (ATV) and industrial power segments still represent over 50% of revenue and are grappling with EV demand normalization and customer inventory digestion. Additionally, large-scale capex in the Dresden smart power fab and Kulim Malaysia cleanrooms creates near-term margin drag if non-AI semiconductor end-markets remain soft. IFNNY is tracked on the evaluation list to monitor whether AI power inflection can outpace automotive cyclical drag.
key_driver: AI data center power delivery ramp (>€2.5B FY26) + vertical VRMs vs automotive & industrial cycle recovery

thesis_breakers_qualitative: AI data center power delivery revenue stalls below €2.0B in FY26 due to design loss to MPWR or discrete GaN competitors
Automotive chip demand experiences multi-quarter double-digit contraction without second-half recovery
Dresden or Kulim fab ramp suffers severe operational delays or cost overruns that compress company gross margin below 36%
Chinese domestic power semiconductor manufacturers capture meaningful market share in standard EV and solar inverters
Customer capacity reservation agreements unravel or advance payments are refunded due to AI infrastructure capex digestion

break_rules.narrative: Infineon revenue contracting >10% YoY for 2 consecutive quarters indicates severe cyclical downturn.
Gross margin falling below 36% indicates severe fab underutilization or pricing collapse.
Operating margin below 10% signals severe structural operating deleverage.
